utterances.text: On what grounds would those people be brought in? On the basis of what information? Would that be an order issued by the police station commander or operative information?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A list of suspects would be drawn up based on operative information. There would be a list of persons suspected of having committed a criminal offence or being involved in a terrorist group. IDs would be checked, and those people would be brought in for interviews.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those interviews would then be conducted by police inspectors at the headquarters of the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and they were not limited to Jasovic and Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many inspectors were there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the department for crime prevention, there were a number of inspectors. All of them were involved in this work, including Jasovic and Sparavalo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This information under tab 13, is that an original document of your Secretariat of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read this report at the time when it was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did each of these reports have to be submitted to you for your consideration?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of them had to be submitted to me, and I decided to what authorities they would be forwarded, whether to the State Security Service or the staff of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the staff in Serbia, the ministry staff in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move now to tab 14. We have a statement here. Is that an original document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Jasovic binder?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which was admitted already?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to read this statement at the time when it was taken from the person signed?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- in fact, I am certain that I read this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should have a translation, then. Could the court deputy find out. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this statement make reference to any terrorist activity or the presence of people involved in terrorist activities in the village of Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who gave this statement claims that they saw Afet Bilali, Rifat Imeri and Nusret Musliu wearing KLA uniforms. All of these people were natives of Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read paragraph 4. I don't want to spend too much time on this. What does he say? The paragraph begins with the words: "In the month of December ..."

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In December this year, in the village of Racak, I saw Afet Bilali Rifat Imeri and Nusret Musliu wearing uniforms with KLA insignia and carrying automatic rifles. I was in Racak for the last time on the 18th of December, 1998, where, on the road leading to the mosque in Racak, I saw four persons wearing KLA uniforms, or uniforms with KLA insignia, and carrying automatic rifles. I recognised Isljama Imeri from Racak village."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the basis of similar statements, would you establish the composition, the strength, and the type of activities engaged in by the KLA in a particular area?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But also on the basis of other types of information we would receive, not only in the statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Look at tab 15. Do you see there a statement that is another document from your Secretariat of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not also admitted through Jasovic? If so, what's the point of going all over it again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The point is that Mr. Janicevic, who was chief of that Secretariat of the Interior, might confirm whether this is an authentic document of his Secretariat of the Interior in view of the information contained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ask specific questions which Mr. Janicevic could answer with his personal knowledge and which cannot be dealt with through Mr. Jasovic. Time is very precious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, did you read this statement at the time when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have any importance to you, as chief of the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it had importance. We had a number of terrorists whose presence was established in the village of Racak, headed by the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, could you give us a comprehensive knowledge how much it's duplicated with Jasovic exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've tracked -- tab 15 is 1.55 in Jasovic. Tab 16 is tab 1.8 in Jasovic, and that's as far as it goes. We haven't been able to find any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please let us know as soon as you find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is a translation of tab 14 in the Jasovic binders. Ms. Higgins has done copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on very quickly. We dealt with these statements and report already.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I will be asking only short questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, under tab 16 there is another statement. Is that an authentic document of your Secretariat of the Interior? Please look at the statement.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at it now. It is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read it at the time when it was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It was taken together with members of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what basis do you claim that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because among the signatures we see the signature of Srboljub Vojinovic, who was representing the state security sector in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, did we not deal with all the statements or reports taken by or written by Mr. Jasovic? Did we? And this should have been included in Jasovic exhibits or in Stevanovic exhibits, given the number tab 305. You should be aware of this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I have in front of me the former chief of Urosevac SUP, and I'm seeking confirmation of authenticity of documents originating from his secretariat, his former secretariat, and I'm asking him whether he had seen them at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Move on very quickly and get to Racak event as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you the same request about the statement in tab 17: Is that an authentic document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No record in Jasovic of tab 17, as far as we can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Stevanovic? Please do so, yes. Thank you. Next question, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just pausing there. Tab 17, unless others have it, there is no translation. While I'm on my feet: The translations that have been given out this morning I gather mean that we now have different translations of that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. document. I think this morning may be different from the one in the Jasovic binder. It's a small point, but it's something to have in mind. But in any case, no translation for 17 and we haven't seen this document before. I haven't yet been able to check whether the names are apparently significant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're saying that there are translations given to you for which ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it was 16.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 16, and I think -- 15, I beg your pardon. 15. We've now got two different translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, are they materially different?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I don't know yet, I haven't checked, but we're not being provided the same document. More significant, 17, no translation, is the problem for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have it either, but that can be sorted out later, whether they were the ones exhibited already or not. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under tab 17 are persons listed from the village of Racak who are said to be members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 22nd November 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you already confirmed the authenticity of this document from your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you narrow down the area where this terrorist brigade was active?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The so-called 161st Terrorist Brigade of the KLA was active in the area of Stimlje and the area of Urosevac. The area of Stimlje covers the following villages: Racak, Petrovo, Belince, Crnoljevo, Laniste, Topilo, Devecak, Malopoljce, Muzicane, Racince [phoen], Petrovic, Gornje Godance, Donje Godance, Zborce and Petrastica. And of course Crnoljevo and the Crnoljevo gorge, the entire gorge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned a moment ago that from the Crnoljevska gorge you see the road to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which area was this brigade of the KLA active?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Municipality of Kacanik and municipality of Strpce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Ivaja, area of Kacanik. The commander was Ibri Razi [phoen], also known as Bardi [phoen]. He also died in a fight with our security forces. He was replaced by Dzabir Zarko. In addition to that base of the brigade, which was in Ivaja, the brigade had its sub-staffs in villages. Vodenica, Bob, Icevac, Kovacevac, Dubrava, Slatina, and other villages where they also had their sub-staffs but with a smaller number of members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think there's something missing from the transcript. Are we now dealing with a different brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I put a question that had to do with the 162nd Brigade, and a few moments ago we were dealing with the 161st Brigade. And what the witness said now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't appear in the transcript that you've moved on to the 162nd [Realtime transcript read in error "161nd"] Brigade, although it's obvious from the answers that we're dealing with something different. And indeed, the transcript is now compounded it by calling it the "161nd Brigade." It should be the 162nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That having been clarified, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, please look at tab 18, or rather, 18, 18.1, 18.2, and so on. What kind of documents are these? Please look at 18.1. It is a statement taken from Adem Salahu, from the village of Bicevac, municipality of Kacanik. Jasovic and Sparavalo took the statement, as well as Nebojsa Djordjevic, who works for state security, and it was done, therefore, together with the RDB, the state security of the Republic. In this statement, we have a long list of KLA members, because they say that the following members took part in the KLA activities.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this arrested KLA member gives a list of his colleagues from the KLA on several pages of this statement.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell us the circumstances in which this person came to give the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person was brought in to custody by the police, or rather, brought in for an interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The suspicion was that he was a member of the terrorist organisation of the KLA. Later on, as he made his statement and gave his interview, that proved to be true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And was action taken against him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I cannot remember now, but I think that he was remanded into custody and handed over to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it usual for your inspector to take a statement together with a person from state security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When terrorism is concerned, there were cases when statements were taken together, and it was advisable, because members of the State Security Service had more information about the terrorist organisations, groups, and individuals who were active in that way. That would make the statement proper and in that way the statement could lead to proceedings being initiated against such persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when this statement was taken, did you have the opportunity of seeing it, reading it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the opportunity of seeing it, reading it, familiarising myself with its content, and it was also sent to the MUP headquarters, in addition to being sent further on to the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, Mr. Janicevic: What does the document contained in tab 18.2 relate to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can tab 18.1 be an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And can tab 17 be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Was it not included in the Jasovic binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I haven't been able to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have to deal with it. We have to hear from Mr. Nice on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 18.1 is, to my recollection, clearly new. I could be wrong, but I simply don't recall seeing any kind of statement with a list of names of that length. I don't at the moment recall and can't find the person named Adem Salahu being dealt with. We don't have a translation and it may be that this one should be marked for identification at most at this stage. But I would also ask the Chamber to consider requiring of the accused to identify any of these names on the list that he says are of particular significance. Of course, we can go through the names and calculate for him which, if any, of these names he now says are of significance, but he should, frankly, be doing that for us. And simply to come to that at the end of the whole exercise of the case and find that these names are drawn out would not be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What would you mean by saying that to mark for identification? Until what? Until when?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, certainly until we've got a translation but possibly also until I've asked questions about it, because I don't know what I'm going to say yet about this statement or its reliability. How can I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No further objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, but that objection is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Subject to your inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification, as was suggested. And if Mr. Milosevic could identify important names among this list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the witness, Mr. Janicevic, to look at tab 18.1, which contains the statement made by this KLA member who was brought in by the police and interviewed to indicate certain names that he considers to be important on this list, the persons who are mentioned as members of the KLA, that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the most important names is Camilj Iljazi, nicknamed Barli, who was commander of the 161st Brigade. After all, all of these names are important because all these people were members of a terrorist organisation that operated in the area, together with their commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Look at tab 18.2 now. This is an official note which does not come from the Ministry of the Interior. What is this? What does this pertain to? Please be so kind as to explain.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This note pertains to the area of the villages of Ivaja and Kotlina. I received information from the MUP staff of the Republic of Serbia that allegedly a massacre had been committed in the area against civilians. Since this was an area where the military was in charge, I asked the commander of the 243rd Brigade to inform me as to whether there was anything going on there that would be of security interest, and I also asked whether a massacre had been committed at all. My request was responded to by way of this note. I think there's a translation here. Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that you found out from this note that you received from Lieutenant Colonel Djurovic? I see that he signed it. Or rather, somebody else signed on his behalf. I can't read the signature, though.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out that in the area of Ivaja and Kotlina, there was a mop-up operation. The Siptar terrorist gangs were mopped up within a five-kilometre area. The 243rd Motorised Brigade took part in it, and also the PJP, the special purposes unit from Urosevac. And some members of the police station in Kacanik. The action was carried out according to a plan of the 243rd Brigade, or rather, the border battalion of that brigade. They informed me that they do not have any information about the loss of life of a large number of civilians in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained just now that you were actually checking information that you received from the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you sought an explanation from the military commander in charge of the area?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer was negative?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the passage I note that there were three young women who were armed and partly dressed in uniforms. Did you know that at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew about it as soon as I received this official note. Three younger women who were armed and partly dressed in uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would there be an on-site investigation of these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After every anti-terrorist action carried out by the MUP or the military in the area of the secretariat where I was head of secretariat, always - and I emphasise always - an on-site investigation was carried out. The investigating judge and the scene-of-crime officers always went there and documented it by photographs and video as well. Everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did that happen in relation to the event of the 9th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So there must be a report of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So why did you have to ask the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because in the reports that I received, there was no information like the kind the staff was seeking from me, so I wanted to double-check to see whether something had been omitted, whether there was any omission on the part of the persons who were there. The scene-of-crime officer who was there had not informed me that a large number of civilians had lost their lives, so I was wondering whether there had been an omission, whether something had been done in that way. I don't know whether I'm being clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is clear, but by the 8th of May, when this report was written, there had already been an investigation by your officers and an investigating judge had been to carry out an on-site investigation; have I got that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The investigating judge went out the same day when the terrorist action was over. Our report to the MUP staff went on the same day when the action was completed, or rather, when I received the report of the on-site investigation from the scene-of-crime officers. This report probably went through some other channels, or rather, this report about the killing of a larger number of civilians probably went through the Verification Mission. So already on the next day, the 9th or the 10th, I cannot recall the exact date, I wrote to the commander of the 243rd Motorised Brigade, asking him whether he had any information to that effect. It was only on the 8th of May that I received a reply, a reply to my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it took him more than three weeks to reply to you? Rather unsatisfactory. Anyway, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note several statements taken by Mr. Jasovic are following this tab, so this -- so I take it that this official note was based upon those investigations by Jasovic. Is it right? From tab 18 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what number you're referring to exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From 18.3 until 18. -- I don't know how long it goes. A number of statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know which particular note you're referring to, I beg your pardon. The one that we've been dealing with until now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The official note, tab 18.2, was written on 8th of May, 1999. The following tab, which was not dealt with yet by the accused, is a statement taken by Mr. Jasovic on 1st of May. So when you referred to on-site investigation, do you mean this kind of investigation by Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just have a look at this. 18.2 has nothing to do with what Jasovic did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could take a look at 18.3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see no similarity here, nor do I see any link between this note compiled by Lieutenant Colonel Djurovic and the one taken -- the statement taken by Jasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll leave it to the accused. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can 18.2 be an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're still dealing with 18.2, what does 18.2 say towards the end of the second paragraph? It says that investigators from the MUP of Urosevac carried out the on-site investigation. That's what you said a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the basis of the on-site investigation and all the information you received, you did not know of the loss of lives of many civilians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you say that from the MUP staff, you were asked to resolve the question whether this information about the killing of civilians was correct.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And since I could not deal with the issue through my own people, who were on the ground, because they told me that no civilians were practically killed, I sought additional information. I asked the military to tell me whether it was the situation or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the military told you that it was not correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, with a bit of a delay, but the military told me that what was contained in that other information was not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The statement that we have in tab 18.3, taken by Jasovic, Sparavalo and Zoran Djordjevic -- Jasovic and Sparavalo we have encountered on several occasions, Jasovic testified here, but who is Djordjevic Zoran?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the State Security Service of the Urosevac department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is another example where they took the statements together. Now what does this statement refer to and is this an authentic document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an authentic document and it relates to the identification of individuals who were members of the terrorist organisation of the KLA in the Kacanik area. The villages mentioned are Nika, Kovacevac. That's all I can see here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity of reading the statement at the time it was taken?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite certainly I did, but it's been six or seven years since then, so I can't remember all the details of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know the circumstances in which the person came to give the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't say here. It doesn't state the circumstances, but probably they were taken into custody by the police who were in the checkpoint at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And does it follow you won't know what happened to him afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After giving the statement, the person was probably allowed to go home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All you can say is that this is authentic document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you bring this document with you when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How did you get this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I got the document from the forward command post of the Urosevac SUP in Leskovac -- relocated command post. And part of the documents were given me by the MUP, from the KiM document, Kosovo and Metohija document, the group determining responsibility and accountability of both Albanians and Serbs for the events in Kosovo. And they amass all the relevant information and evidence in order to process the matter further one day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 18.4 is a very brief statement. Who is this third person that signed the statement?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Darko Amanovic, a member of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a statement taken together by the public and State Security Services; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this one about? What does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to persons who had collected money for the needs of the so-called KLA, for its functioning or for the procurement and purchase of the weapons, pursuant to an order by Rufki Suma from the village of Dimce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says which KLA members he knows; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Rufki Suma was also the commander of the local staff for Palivodenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this again an authentic document by your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can tab 18.4 be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any observation from Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to all this material, I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In relation to all this material, I've laid out principal objections earlier and the Chamber has made its ruling about in principle admissibility. I'm not going to repeat those. Where there are no translations, I obviously make the objection that I made earlier on this morning. And as to the documents that are admitted, should of course the Chamber find itself in a position following cross-examination to take the view that documents, once admitted, should be -- should not have been admitted, it's always in a position to change its mind. So the best thing is that, save for those that aren't translated, if we just allow them in on the basis that the Chamber has been allowing them in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of course the matter -- the weight is for the Chamber to decide later. We'll admit 18.3 and 18.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Tab 17 is still an outstanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 17 and 18.1 would be marked for identification. Can we deal with it? Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, in tab 18.5 we have a document which I'm also going to ask you about to ask you whether it is the authentic document of your secretariat and what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an authentic by my secretariat and it relates to persons who collected -- or rather, persons who joined up with the KLA and who engaged in mobilisation, the mobilisation and recruitment of new members for that same organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document in tab 18.6 is another short statement. Is that an authentic document of your secretariat as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can 18.5 be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll deal with it after 18 is over, comprehensively. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In 18.6, the person giving the statement, and it was given on the 14th of April, 1999, he says that at the time there were over 500 KLA members in that particular village.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the information we had at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we come to 18.7A. Is that once again a document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is another secretariat document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we have stipulated here members of the KLA in the Slatina and Ivaja area?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were seven individuals here who were members of the terrorist KLA organisation in Krivaja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one is 18A. Is that an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It relates to the Kacanik municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it is about an attack -- or describes an attack on members of the police station of Kacanik, or rather, the commander, and who might have been in the group -- the perpetrators of the group, and also it refers to the funeral of one of the attackers, Asim Hetem -- Asaj Hetem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a statement with respect to a terrorist operation and the perpetrators thereof; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you arrived at that information by interviewing the person who gave this particular statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was within the frameworks of the investigation that was conducted with respect to the terrorist attack; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is also an official document of your secretariat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we can go on to tab 18.9, which is another statement which should come from your secretariat. The date is the 6th of April. Do you know about this statement?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is a document belonging to my secretariat, and it refers to members of the terrorist KLA organisation who, without uniforms -- were active without uniforms, bearing weapons, wearing civilian clothes in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, this is described as a preliminary interview. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An informative interview. Perhaps the translation is wrong, because here it says -- it uses the usual term, "informativni razgovor," the customary term for "interview." So perhaps that's a matter of the way in which the document was translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask the interpreter whether that one begins in exactly the same way as tab 18. The translation of tab 18 is: "On 13 April 1999 an interview was conducted ..." and this one starts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we put the 18.8 and 18.9 together, or the interpreter could note that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the same term, "informativni razgovor," was used in both statements, which equals "interview."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I thank the interpreters for their effort. That has been clarified. Thank you. Let's proceed. Mr. Janicevic, when your inspectors take a witness statement from a witness, do they produce the statements in Cyrillic letters or in alphabet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It depends on the typewriters they had. Some had Cyrillic-script typewriters, others had Latin-script typewriters. Jasovic mostly used the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I don't think I saw witness Jasovic's statements written in Cyrillic letters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jasovic's typewriter was a Latin-script typewriter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that's why I'm asking. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. 18.10 is the next one. What does that tell us? And I can see that it is a statement which was typed out in the Cyrillic script on the 26th of March, 1999. Is that an authentic document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is another authentic document by the Secretariat of the Interior of Urosevac. It talks about an interview with Ljaci Naser from the village of Pustenik in the Kacanik municipality. And he goes on to say in his statement that in the village of -- in Kacanik municipality, the 161st Brigade was formed, led by Camilj Iljazi, nicknamed Barli, and another person. And they say that in certain hamlets or villages in that municipality, a number of village staffs were established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, how can you say this is an authentic document? I note Jasovic's and Sparavalo's signatures are missing here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since this has been photocopied a number of times, maybe you can't see the signatures, but the document is authentic 100 per cent. I'm quite sure of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can note the witness's signature, while we cannot see the signatures of the inspectors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They're not visible here. But probably it was signed. But as I say, because of the photocopying, you can't see the signatures. But the document is 100 per cent authentic, because we see here members of the KLA, persons who were members of the KLA. For example, in line 6 or 7, his nickname was Era, and he is in prison at the moment in Pristina for having committed the crime of murder, and the International Court in Pristina, in March this year, tried the case, and many others too from the Kacanik area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it of any importance, this fact that Mr. Kwon pointed out to us, that is to say that, for the most part, or most of the statements so far taken by Jasovic were typed out in the Latin script, whereas this one was typed out in the Cyrillic script. Is that of any importance?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really, because our service used both official scripts. The Cyrillic and Latin were both official scripts, so it depended on the typewriter that people had. And Jasovic probably was in the Kacanik area when taking this statement and this kind of typewriter happened to be there, so he had to type the statement out on that particular typewriter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, what about the statement in tab 18.11? Is that an original document of your Secretariat of the Interior, and what does that one refer to?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another authentic document of the Secretariat of the Interior of Urosevac, signed by Jasovic and Sparavalo, and it is about the fact that the villagers of the village of Ivaja left their houses. And a local, Halati [phoen], took to the forest. And it mentions an individual whom he met in the forest with an automatic rifle, and that members of the MUP carried such rifles, which meant that Alji Ljuta had seized the rifle from one of the MUP members who had probably been killed in the fighting against the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janicevic. Now we move on to tab 18.12, where we have another statement. Is that also an authentic document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is an authentic document of the Urosevac SUP. The statement was taken by Jasovic and Sparavalo, and it is about Rafiz -- yes. Members of the KLA. Azem Elezi, who mobilised some members of the KLA. Sometimes that mobilisation was done forcibly, with threats issued, under duress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this person giving the statement was said to be -- was accused of being a Serb spy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know how this person came to be in the police office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He probably came on his own, of his own accord, from what I can read in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under tab 18.13, we see a statement related to the murder of the commander of the police station of Kacanik, who was killed at the entrance to the Gajre village, Kacanik municipality. Is this an authentic statement and a document of your secretariat, dated the 20th March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an authentic statement from the SUP of Urosevac. This one was also taken by Jasovic and Sparavalo. It was given by Izahir Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mulaki. He describes the way in which this murder was planned. They called the commander on his cellphone and told him that Riza Kiki, a person from the local security, had been kidnapped. The commander did not suspect anything. He went out to check this information, he was ambushed on the road and three members of the police who accompanied him were also killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the gravest incident just before the NATO aggression in your area?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the most serious one, not only in my area, but in the area of Kacanik until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Janicevic, what proportion of these various people giving statements could speak Serb, the Serb language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 99 per cent of them. 99 per cent of all persons who have given these statements speak Serbian. Over 80 per cent of the overall ethnic Albanian population in the Urosevac area speaks Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And in what language would most of them actually give the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those who did not understand Serbian would give their statements in Albanian. Those who understood Serbian would give their statements in Serbian, on a case-to-case basis, whatever the interviewee asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, if you could tell us where this evidence leads us. Suppose that they all -- the content of all these documents, statements, are true. What does it prove? Does it have any bearing in relation to the specific event referred to in the indictment or as in Racak case? These names appear in the Schedule L of the Kosovo indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, Kacanik is part of what you call the indictment, and this attests to the fact that -- sorry. The indictment alleges that a certain number of civilians were killed by the state security forces, whereas these documents speak about great presence of the KLA in that area and very intensive terrorist activities, including murders and attacks on policemen, soldiers, civilians. This absolutely refutes all the claims about the terrorising of civilians in the area of Kacanik municipality, as you have already seen. The witness we have before us, former chief of Urosevac SUP, verified the information that he would receive from outside. He did not rely on each piece of information he would receive. He would sometimes seek additional confirmation even from military authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My question was specifically whether any of these alleged KLA members appear as victims in the indictment. Schedule L deals with the victims in relation to Kacanik municipality. So you're not alluding to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not compare that schedule with all these statements, because my time is very limited, but I will do so. In fact, I will ask one of my associates to cross-check to see if any of the persons mentioned in the statements are on the list. My point is, and my assertion is, that neither the police nor the army committed any crimes, in that municipality or in any other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we can deal with these documents much faster. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I would like to draw your attention to the claims made by a number of witnesses who testified here, very authentically, who spoke about the number of Albanians killed in this period by the KLA. That is an aspect that is given short shrift here from the word go. More of them were killed from June 1999 onwards than in the preceding period, many more, in the period when there were no police or army left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, what do we see under tab 18.14? I see it's an official note, but I won't go on, in order to avoid leading you.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official note drawn up by authorised officer Boban Krstic. It mentions persons who are members of the KLA who were active in Bob and Ivaja villages. Reference is made to their names. Rahim Elezi, Adami Zekerija, the son of a certain Imer Gasi, et cetera. This is also an authentic document of the secretariat in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the official note under 18.15 about? Is it an authentic document of your secretariat? In fact, it says here "Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, Secretariat in Urosevac, Kacanik Police Station."

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This official note was submitted by the deputy commander of the Kacanik Police Station, to the effect that a certain Sulejman Loki from Kotlina village came of his own accord to this police station, and he stated that a group of four armed men in camouflage uniforms and hoods on their heads, with KLA insignia, came and took his hunting rifle. That means that in the period before the war, the terrorists used to disarm all the people, Albanian people, who possessed weapons legally. We had hundreds of such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is also authentic as a document?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say the same about tab 18.16? I mean about authenticity.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The authorised officers are different in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... questions and answers, leading or otherwise, about authentic. It may be that we should know what is being meant by "authentic." Does it mean that the witness produced them himself or is positively affirming that they are documents which come from a certain source, or does it mean something else? I'm not sure what it means. I'm not particularly being difficult, I just want to know what is being meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it that the witness brought with him these documents. Am I right in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And it was in the official archive in Urosevac police -- SUP Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was in the official archive of Urosevac SUP and the area of the police station itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You saw these documents contemporaneously at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kwon just raised an issue concerning these documents that you brought and that are being kept in the archives. Were all the documents preserved or were a part of them destroyed, lost?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only a small portion of all the documents were preserved. The greatest part of them were destroyed or they were left behind in the area, in the localities of the particular police stations or the Urosevac SUP. After the withdrawal of the police, following the agreement, our police force handed over their building to KFOR, and we don't know what happened to the documentation that was left behind. Some documents were destroyed in April 1999, when the SUP building was bombed. The entire building burnt down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the MUP building in the centre of Pristina was destroyed by the bomb, were other buildings around it also damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many other buildings were destroyed. The municipality building, part of the provincial Assembly building was destroyed, a great number of enterprises and factories, the Orthodox Christian cemetery, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also mention the post office?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The post office building was among the first to be bombed in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know you said that, but it's missing from the transcript. I think you should speak more distinctly, and speak up, generally. If the interpreters don't hear you, it won't be on the record.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to speak too loud, not to offend the Judges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I heard you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it's a convenient time. I note the time. We'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, in document 18.6, there is an official note. What does it refer to? Is it another document of your secretariat? What is it about? What are the events concerned? Let me draw your attention to the effect that there is a link between 18.16 and 18.17.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It seems to be 18.16. There is no microphone for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The official note was drawn up on the premises of SUP Urosevac regarding the kidnapping of Agim Idrizi from Laniste village, Kacanik municipality. That person was kidnapped by six members of the terrorist KLA who came to his house by night, dragged him out of his bed, handcuffed him, and took him away, telling his mother that they were taking him to fight against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 5th of March, I believe. Yes. On the 5th of March, at 9.00 p.m., in the area of Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this official note in 18.16, it says the person is still suffering from depression, is unable to remember everyone he had seen, and then there is an additional statement, a supplementary statement, under 18.17.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the kidnapping, that person was taken to the KLA prison in Ivaja village that was attached to the headquarters of the 161st Brigade. After the anti-terrorist operation of the 8th of March, 1999, some of the persons who had been kidnapped were freed. However, this person, together with some others, were taken, transferred to an auxiliary prison. They were taken from village to village, ending up in Raka. And then a vehicle came to pick them up from Raka and take them to the central KLA prison in Lapusnik. I'm not reading from this, I am recollecting that on the road to Llapusnik, he and four other persons, somewhere around Kosin village, because that's the only place where there is a crossing over the river, he fell out from that jeep, together with another person, Nezir -- I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a particular relevance to all this, Mr. Milosevic? It just seems to me to be wasting time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us establish just one more thing, Mr. Bonomy. It is relevant that the KLA terrorised Albanians at the time, very intensively so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at page 2, towards the bottom. It says: "On the same night, half an hour later, they took us to Bicevac village, where I saw 50 members of the KLA and recognised Dzevat Belja carrying a weapon and a certain Hajrulah, nicknamed Butcher." Then these people were taken to the headquarters. All this happened in mid-March 1999. Then he speaks about the torture they were subjected to. On the next page, he says -- they ask him whether he was from the State Security Service. "I answered that I sold firewood. And after that, he put a hook through my nostril and started beating me. And then again caught me with a hook on my lower lip." There is reference to all sorts of terror imposed on Albanians in the area from which this witness comes from. Let us not waste any more time. What do we see under tab 18.18? Reference is made to some important person, a commander or something.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is about Rufki Suma, who was the self-styled commander of the KLA staff for the territory of Pustenik, that is, the local community of Djeneral Jankovic, Kacanik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anything about that KLA commander?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rufki Suma was the commander of the KLA staff for Pustenik village. Yes, yes. We had prior information about him, that he was engaged in hostile -- organised hostile activities and had made public appearances. In 1998, when the State Security Service identified the first illegal staff of the KLA for Kacanik, Rufki Suma was in the group that was arrested, but under circumstances that had not been clarified until the end, he managed to escape. Eventually, criminal proceedings were instigated against him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under 18.19, do we see another statement? Is it authentic? It was given by Baskim Celaki.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an authentic document. Baskim Celaki was a member -- in fact, he was suspected to be a KLA member, but it was never proved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In 18.20, we see another reference to Rufki Suma. It says: "This staff was formed by Rufki Suma, from Dimce village, Kacanik municipality."

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what extent was the KLA present in Kacanik municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost until the end of 1998. The KLA was present in Kacanik municipality without being active, without taking any actions against the army, the police, or civilians. The intensity of their activity started to grow in the beginning of January. That happened with the first kidnappings of Albanians who did not support KLA policies and did not support their cause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What about these documents in 18.21, 22, and 23? These are statements by Busi Refik, Brava Sehat and Busi Zajedin. They all date back to March 1999 and relate to KLA activities. Are they among the authentic documents from your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are all original and authentic documents of Urosevac SUP.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender these collectively, Mr. Kwon. You said you would deal with that after we finish with tab 18. It is my request that these documents be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All tabs will be admitted except for tab 18.13 and 18.19, which were not translated, and will be marked for identification, pending translation. And I note tab 17 was translated and handed over to the Chamber, so that can be admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, as briefly as possible, what do you know about 163rd Brigade? You mentioned 161st and 162nd, with an emphasis on the 161st. What do you know about 163rd?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That brigade of the KLA was formed only on paper. A commander was appointed. That was Ahmed Kaciko [phoen], who got killed in fights with the state security forces -- security forces, rather. And for a long time after that, until just before the war, they did not have the commander, and then they got a commander who used to be a deputy commander of the police station in Strpce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the first serious attacks on the area -- in the area of Urosevac SUP happen?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1987 [as interpreted], in November, when David Dugoli was killed, or rather --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dalip Dugoli, an Albanian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the background of his liquidation?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The background was that he did not want to join this terrorist organisation, he did not pay the so-called tax to them. He was an active socio-political worker, or official, and he used to say that the terrorists, those people who went to the woods, are the worst kind of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. criminals. And he said that in every gathering with his friends, and even before his enemies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, are we hearing the events in 1987? Can we move on to 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't ask a question linked to 1987. I asked when the first more serious terrorist attacks took place in the Urosevac SUP area, and the witness's answer was that was the killing of the Albanian at the end of 1997. Now, whether that was intensified in 1998 and 1999 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a mistake in the transcript. There's a mistake in the transcript that's causing the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened, then, in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, the attacks became more intense and there were preparations for more serious terrorist attacks at the beginning of January, when an explosive was used to attack a house in which a member of the State Security Service, Rajko Dodik [phoen], was living, belonging to the Urosevac SUP. He was a lodger there. That was in January. Then in April, another explosive device was launched against another policeman, traffic policeman, Miljam Veljkovic [phoen] his name was, and the attack became intensified on the road running from Stimlje to Suva Reka, in the Fermilje [phoen] gorge, in mid-1998. And from that time, in fact, the terrorist acts and provocation in the area became constant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what do the documents in tabs 19 and 20 relate to? Perhaps we can take a look at them together. They date to the second half of 1998, as far as I can see, the statements.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the minutes or records taken from individuals who were interviewed by the State Security Service for having prepared terrorist attacks, and they are individuals who organised the first terrorist staff in the Urosevac area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both these two statements, the one in tab 20 and the one in tab 19, do they both relate to the same activity, to the same action?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both relate to the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, the people giving the statement are different. Different people gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But otherwise, the event was the same, the subject matter was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, a new problem with these statements, I suppose, these documents, at any event. Before I come to that point, I ought to just make one point that I've been meaning to make earlier. I haven't taken objection to the, in principle, to the production of the earlier documents coming from Jasovic and Sparavalo because they were admitted not only through Jasovic but also at the hands of one or two other witnesses. But of course, it is, on topics of weight, a matter of concern that these weren't dealt with when Jasovic was here himself. I just put that on the record. So far as 19 and 20 are concerned, 19 has not only the problem of being untranslated but of being significantly, I think, illegible. One does one's best. I think it's going to be tricky to read that text, and I don't know what the translators will make of it. From my point of view, it's also unfortunate that the names of the officials taking the statement are not at present identified, or maybe they are, but I'd be very much assisted by knowing who it was who did take them, because at the moment the names are, I think, illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us ask the witness whether he can identify the authorised official who took these statements, both of them, 19 and tab 20 as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In tab 19, one of the signatories was the official Srdjan Rosic, authorised official, the second one. I can't make out the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is Srdjan Rosic?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdjan Rosic at that time was the operative worker of the state security department of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a document of your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the State Security Service document which was sent to us to keep us informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in your area?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what about tab 20? Tab 20 I can see has been translated. Tab 20. Let's just have a look. I think that the signatory was Dragan Djordjevic. Once again, a worker of the State Security Service department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Milosevic. Judge Bonomy has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What action was taken against these people once they had confessed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since they confessed, a criminal report was raised against them and there were orders to arrest them from the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Then what would happen to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then they would go to prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But do you not know what actually happened? Was there a trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. By handing him over to the investigating judge, along with the papers, that's where the Ministry of the Interior's work ceases. We handed everything over. If the person was sentenced, then we would receive a judgement with the sentence back to us and it would be recorded in the SUP archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And after June 1999, were you in a position to receive such reports back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After June 1999, for Kosovo and Metohija, there were no court cases at all, as far as I know, so we did not receive any reports of that kind back. All the cases that were tried in Kosovo and Metohija in the courts there remained in the courts, and the cases that were with the prosecutor remained there, the pending cases in the secretariats remained in the secretariats of the interior, the analysis department, and it was the position that no documents should be taken away and out of the buildings in which the work was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was it you had to move from your office in Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 17th of April I moved to Pristina. The paper was dated the 15th, but I handed over my duties and left Pristina on that date. I didn't have an office there because the SUP building was bombed and completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And does that mean that, by that time, no report had come back of any action taken in court against either of these two persons who gave the statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, while a court case is pending, it is not -- they're not duty-bound to inform the Ministry of the Interior what is happening to the accused and whether they did stand accused. I repeat: It was our task and job to see that persons who were dealt with by the crime technicians and criminal reports filed and arrested, and then all the papers were given -- handed up to the investigating judge, who then decided whether the individuals were arrested and remanded in custody. There would be a deadline 30 days, 60 days, depending on the crime committed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. It would be very helpful to me to have this sort of thing followed through so that I get a complete picture of what actually happened to people who made such confessions of involvement with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, I take it that all you know in relation to this document is that this statement was sent to you from state security, so you do not know the situation how this witness was taken to the custody of state security and what happened to this witness later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what happened because there was a uniform system for the criminal reports filed and written out in the secretariats and then sent to the investigating judges, courts, and prosecutors. They go via the public security system, which is a joint service, a communal service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is just speculation as well. But did you bring these documents with you in person as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that is a copy which is sent from the state security at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, you said a moment ago that the criminal report itself is filed by the Secretariat of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is your organ; right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat of the Interior sends on the criminal report to the competent investigating judge of the prosecuting office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that document, formally speaking and officially speaking, must pass through your organs?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it must pass through my organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This related to the intensification of terrorist attacks in 1998. Tell us, please: Terrorist attacks of this kind, did they continue in 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. In the second half of 1998, there was not a day that went by without terrorist action and provocation, especially in the Stimlje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the situation like -- what was the situation like after the establishment of the Verification Mission, at the end of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle of 1998, a number of anti-terrorist actions were launched in which the combat capabilities of the KLA were eliminated throughout Kosovo mostly. Those forces were routed. Some of them were dispelled, dispersed, some were arrested. What remained took to the hills and mountains, and I'm talking about the area covered by my secretariat there. They went to villages which were almost inaccessible, such as Devetak, Topilo, and the upper part of the village of Jezerce. After the establishment of the Verification Mission, and when it started working, that is to say, sometime up until the end of October 1998, there was a repeated takeover of positions where the terrorists had been previously, up until the end of the anti-terrorist operations. Those positions were taken up again, as were the positions held by the army of Yugoslavia and the police up until then. Because, pursuant to no agreement with the OSCE, we had to withdraw and to retain only a portion of those defence positions in the area. For example, for the area of Stimlje, Crnoljevska gorge, there were six observation posts and nothing more, except for the regular police stations, for instance. That's as far as the police is concerned. The army had one Combat Group on Canovica hill, right near Stimlje, and two separate combat groups with just a few soldiers manning them, and they were protection for the unit and protection for the settlement of Stimlje itself. One -- on a curve between Belinac and Racak on the road there, that was one, and another Kostanje hill behind Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when the verifiers arrived, the Verification Mission arrived, the attacks became intensified. What were the targets of those attacks in particular?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attacks were targeted at the police forces, the army, citizens, Serbs, Albanians who were not -- or did not want to collaborate with the terrorist organisation and did not wish to offer their assistance. The attacks were also geared against the lines of communication, the roads running to Prizren, or rather, the road from Stimlje to Suva Reka, for instance. So those attacks were such that it was a hit-and-run job from an ambush. They would shoot, kill, and flee from an ambush. After mid-1998, up until the 10th of January, 1999, in that same area, that is to say, the Stimlje area alone, 25 soldiers and civilians were killed; and seriously wounded, 25 soldiers and policemen, or rather, soldiers, policemen, and civilians, which makes a total of about 50 casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at tab 21 now, please, which is a dispatch. It has its number. Just tell us the date of it and what it says in the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispatch or telegram is dated the 28th of February, 1998 [as interpreted]. It is sent by the SUP of Urosevac. I signed it, as head of the secretariat. And I'm informing the MUP of the Republic of Serbia and the staff of the MUP in Pristina that on the 22nd of February, 1999, there was an attack on a patrol which was checking out a piece of information whereby a person was reported kidnapped. And during that attack, the commander of the police station was killed, Captain Bogoljub Staletovic was his name, and some people were wounded: Jankovic Slobodan, Milosavljevic Djordje, and Sladjan Jovanovic. They were wounded on the occasion. In a later attack, in order to pull out the killed commander, Radi and Djuric Zoran, from another part of the unit, was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this actually happen, did you say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, the transcript refers to this document as dated 28th of February, 1998. But instead it should be 1999.
